interest: This document provides insight into the bilateral diplomatic mechanics surrounding the administration of the 1911 North Pacific Fur Seal Convention, under which Japan, the United States, Great Britain/Canada, and Russia cooperated on fur seal conservation and harvest monitoring. Although brief, this cross-reference note shows how Japanese Embassy staff routinely coordinated with Far Eastern Affairs specialist Joseph W. Ballantine regarding annual observation missions to the breeding grounds on Alaska's Pribilof Islands. Furthermore, it serves as a valuable archival index pointing researchers to related diplomatic records filed under decimal 894.628-Vessels/52.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department cross-reference sheet (Document File Note) dated June 5, 1930, cross-referencing decimal file 894.628-Vessels/52. The note records a memorandum delivered to Joseph W. Ballantine of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs by a representative of the Japanese Embassy, advising that Japan would not send an observer to the Pribilof Islands in 1930 to monitor the fur-seal industry.

subfiles.summary: This Document File Note cross-references a memorandum filed under 894.628-Vessels/52 dated June 5, 1930. The memorandum was left with Mr. Ballantine of the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs by a member of the Japanese Embassy. It informs the United States government that Japan would not send a representative to the Pribilof Islands during 1930 to observe the fur-seal industry.
